MAJOR: `_git` now hard-raises on any non-zero rc, and `transitions()` calls `_git("diff", "--name-only", f"{base}..HEAD")` without `allow_fail`; when `merge-base develop HEAD` fails (shallow clone, no local `develop`) the fallback `"origin/develop"` also frequently fails, so the whole gate crashes instead of degrading as before. This is a new CI-fatal path not covered by the regression tests.

Module docstring now promises "JSON report on stdout plus structured JSON event lines on stderr", but the diff contains no corresponding change to `main()`/report emission. If false, doc/behavior mismatch; if true, an unannounced output-contract change that any CI consumer parsing the single stderr line will break on.

`product-forge/config/store-registry.json` adds a bare `"BI-TEST-*.json"` glob to a shipped registry path list, yet the new tests write fixtures only under `tmp_path`. Either the entry is dead config, or it mutates production sync/ignore semantics for every repo-root `BI-TEST-*.json` — test scaffolding leaked into shipped configuration.

`id-blocks.json` jumps `reserved_up_to` from 1469 to 1477 while the only new session claims 1477; IDs 1470–1476 are reserved but owned by no session, i.e. silently leaked or allocated elsewhere without a recorded reservation.
MINOR: Acceptance criterion says `JSONDecodeError` propagates; the implementation wraps it in `RuntimeError`. Fail-closed behavior holds, but the AC's literal contract (and any caller catching the original exception type) is not met.

`transitions()` performs I/O side effects (`print` to stderr) inside what is otherwise a pure library function; test runs emit noise and callers cannot suppress it. Observability belongs at the report layer.

The `_git` fail-closed change applies to every call site in the module, including `audit()`/`--report` paths not covered by the new tests; a previously-tolerated failure there now becomes fatal without test coverage.
`--self-test` negative matrix was not extended for the new failure modes (malformed item, non-object item, repo-root escape), so the escape hatch self-verification is stale.
Broken symlinks raise `FileNotFoundError` and are silently classified as "deleted in the diff", weakening the fail-closed guarantee for an unreadable-but-present path.
NIT: `functools.lru_cache` on `_repo_root()` is fine for a CLI but couples a stateful global to tests that must monkeypatch the symbol rather than the cache; consider injecting the root for clarity.
`rel.replace("\\", "/")` normalization is applied in `transitions()` but not in `_load()`, so an escape check could be bypassed differently on Windows-path inputs; harmless today, worth a comment.
SUMMARY: The core fix (resolve changed items under `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, fail closed on malformed input, skip only deleted paths) is sound, well-tested for the main paths, and satisfies the language rule (tooling Python). Top risks are the new unguarded `git diff` hard-fail crash path, an unverified stdout/stderr contract change in the docstring, test-fixture globs and ID reservations polluting shipped config, and the AC's literal `JSONDecodeError`-propagation requirement being met only semantically.
